title: Notch Filter - Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD) for 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Pierre Dubois

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Notch Filter filter targeting Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD) for 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module. The filter is designed on 42° YX LiTaO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 2591.8 MHz and bandwidth of 131.9 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Notch Filter
- Frequency Band: Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD)
- Application: 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module
- Substrate: 42° YX LiTaO3
- Package: WLP (Wafer Level Package)
- Design Tool: Cadence AWR Microwave Office
- Design Center: Helsinki 5G Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Notch Filter design targeting Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       2591.8 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       131.9 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 1.3 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 8.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 23.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 41.0 dB
Q Factor:               14719
Temperature Coefficient:-25.8 ppm/°C
Die Size:               2.1 x 1.7 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   11
Electrode Material:     Mo/Al
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Cadence AWR Microwave Office and load the Notch Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 42° YX LiTaO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 2591.8 MHz, BW 131.9 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 1.3 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (WLP (Wafer Level Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, 42° YX LiTaO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 7775 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 1.3 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 8.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 198 MHz offset >= 23.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 5 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 8.4 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +26 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 2000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 86%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-08-08
Devices Tested:         72
Insertion Loss (meas):  0.96 dB
Return Loss (meas):     10.5 dB
Rejection (meas):       26.3 dB
Isolation (meas):       46.2 dB
Q Factor (meas):        14719
Group Delay Variation:  1.5 ns
Power Handling:         +27 dBm
Die Yield:              91.5%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Notch Filter design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Rejection at near-band offset requires additional resonator tuning.
d) Simulation-to-measurement correlation was within 3% for all key parameters.
e) No delamination observed after 1000-cycle thermal shock test.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
